daily_life.name: Daily Life & Sunday Routine
daily_life.greeting: Hello! I'm Priya, your Bol speaking coach. How was your day today, and what did you do this morning?
daily_life.greetingHindi: नमस्ते! मैं प्रिया हूँ, आपकी स्पीकिंग कोच। आज आपका दिन कैसा रहा?

turns.transcript: Yesterday I was went to the market for buying fresh vegetables.
turns.reply: That sounds like a lovely Sunday plan! Did you go to the local sabzi mandi or a supermarket?

corrections.original: Yesterday I was went to the market
corrections.better: Yesterday I went to the market
corrections.why: Use simple past 'went' directly without 'was'. हिंदी: 'was went' एक साथ नहीं बोलते — सीधे 'I went' कहें।
Use 'to buy' to express purpose. हिंदी: उद्देश्य बताने के लिए 'to + verb' का उपयोग करें।

turns.encouragement: Good effort! Your sentence was completely clear and understandable.

turns.transcript: I went to local mandi because vegetables is very fresh and cheap there.
turns.reply: I love local mandis too! Which vegetable did you buy the most, and how did you negotiate with the vendor?

corrections.better: I went to the local mandi
corrections.why: Add the article 'the' before specific places like 'the local mandi'.
Use plural verb 'are' with plural noun 'vegetables'.

turns.encouragement: Superb flow! You expressed your reason clearly without hesitation.

turns.transcript: I bought tomatoes and onions, then my mother cooked very tasty sabzi for lunch.
turns.reply: That sounds delicious! Home-cooked meals made with fresh ingredients are the best. What is your favourite dish that your mother makes?

corrections.why: In formal English, you can say 'cooked a delicious curry' or 'cooked a very tasty dish'.

turns.encouragement: Wonderful sentence structure and natural confidence!

interview.name: Job & Placement Interview
interview.greeting: Welcome to your mock interview practice! Tell me a little about yourself and your academic background.
interview.greetingHindi: मॉक इंटरव्यू में स्वागत है! अपने बारे में और अपनी पढ़ाई के बारे में थोड़ा बताएं।

turns.transcript: Myself Rahul, I am doing computer engineering from final year.
turns.reply: Pleasure to meet you, Rahul! What technical project are you currently most proud of?

corrections.better: My name is Rahul / I am Rahul
corrections.why: Avoid starting with 'Myself'. In professional introductions, use 'My name is' or 'I am'.

corrections.original: I am doing computer engineering from final year
corrections.better: I am a final-year Computer Engineering student
corrections.why: More concise and natural in professional interviews.

turns.encouragement: Great composure! Starting an interview takes courage, and you spoke with clarity.

turns.transcript: I builted an AI speaking app that help students to learn English without fear.
turns.reply: That is an impactful problem to solve! How did you handle user audio transcription and feedback generation?

corrections.original: I builted an AI speaking app
corrections.better: I built an AI speaking application
corrections.why: The past tense of build is 'built' (irregular verb), not 'builted'.
Use singular verb 'helps' with singular noun 'app'.

turns.encouragement: Impressive project idea! The interview panel will love this initiative.

travel.name: Travel & Social Settings
travel.greeting: Imagine you've just arrived at a new city's train station. How would you ask someone for directions to the nearest hotel?
travel.greetingHindi: मान लीजिए आप नए शहर के रेलवे स्टेशन पर पहुंचे हैं। होटल का रास्ता कैसे पूछेंगे?

turns.transcript: Excuse me brother, where is the nearest good hotel from here?
turns.reply: Good polite opening! If the person says it's 2 kilometres away, how would you ask about taking an auto or cab?

corrections.why: In professional or travel English, simply 'Excuse me' or 'Excuse me, sir' sounds most natural.

turns.encouragement: Clear, friendly, and practical! You got your question across immediately.

jugaad_genius.name: Jugaad Genius • Everyday Problem Solving
jugaad_genius.greeting: Welcome to Jugaad Genius! Let's test your street-smart problem solving. What would you do if your phone battery drops to 2% right as you need to show your e-ticket at the station gate?
jugaad_genius.greetingHindi: जुगाड़ जीनियस में आपका स्वागत है! मान लीजिए रेलवे स्टेशन पर टिकट दिखाते समय फ़ोन की बैटरी 2% बची है, तो आप टिकट परीक्षक से क्या कहेंगे?
jugaad_genius.greetingTamil: ஜூகாட் ஜீனியஸ் பகுதிக்கு நல்வரவு! ரயில் நிலையத்தில் டிக்கெட் காட்டும் போது பேட்டரி 2% மட்டுமே இருந்தால் எப்படி சமாளிப்பீர்கள்?

turns.transcript: Excuse me sir, my phone battery is at 2 percent, can I quickly scan my ticket before it shuts down?
turns.reply: Brilliant Jugaad composure! Saying 'before it shuts down' conveys the urgency immediately without panic. Next challenge: A shopkeeper gives you toffees instead of 5 rupees change. How do you ask for your cash politely?

corrections.better: may I please quickly scan / could I quickly scan
corrections.why: Using 'could I' or 'may I' is more polite when requesting an urgent exception.

turns.encouragement: Fast, witty thinking! You handled the high-pressure situation like a pro.

turns.transcript: Bhaiya, please give me cash change instead of toffees because I need it for the bus ticket.
turns.reply: Spot-on practical negotiation! Giving a clear real-world reason ('need it for the bus') leaves no room for arguing. Final challenge: Your Wi-Fi disconnected for 30 seconds during an online interview. How do you recover when you reconnect?

corrections.better: could you please give me the cash change
corrections.why: Adding 'could you please' turns a direct demand into a polite yet firm request.

turns.encouragement: Clever and street-smart! Everyday confidence comes from handling these small moments smoothly.

topMistakes: Double past tense ('was went' instead of 'went')
Missing articles ('the local mandi', 'a delicious dish')
Formal intro phrasing ('Myself Rahul' instead of 'My name is Rahul')
defaultSummary.tip: Keep sentences short and punchy. Use simple past tense (went, saw, made) whenever describing yesterday's events.
